### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx`  _(via ReportSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49144fccc873c48babf3c45e56982b6c18169487` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `234d4db624fd235a1501281f7e12006a47ca7bca` — the merge of head `87c194618ca5a40807e3b1a0b8400bda0f1f037f` into base `49144fccc873c48babf3c45e56982b6c18169487`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 234d4db624fd235a1501281f7e12006a47ca7bca && git checkout 234d4db624fd235a1501281f7e12006a47ca7bca
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 49144fccc873c48babf3c45e56982b6c18169487 87c194618ca5a40807e3b1a0b8400bda0f1f037f && git checkout -B drift-repro 49144fccc873c48babf3c45e56982b6c18169487 && git merge --no-ff 87c194618ca5a40807e3b1a0b8400bda0f1f037f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49144fccc873c48babf3c45e56982b6c18169487
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 49144fccc873c48babf3c45e56982b6c18169487` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `87c194618ca5a40807e3b1a0b8400bda0f1f037f`

### ① Derived judgments

Method: card #19856 body + 4 comments read; PR body + diff (5 files vs merge-base `8d1f7ab7`, +306/−5) read in full; `report.zod.ts`, `strict-object.ts`, `metadata-type-schemas.ts`, `metadata-diagnostics.ts`, `stack.zod.ts`, `report.form.ts`, `liveness/report.json` read at the head; objectui `DatasetReportRenderer.tsx` and `ReportDefaultInspector.tsx` read at the `.objectui-sha` pin `f8a9d0fb`; a 22-case `safeParse` probe and the single test file run on a `git archive` of the head under my scratch dir (removed after; probe script + output kept at `review/probe-19856.ts` / `review/probe-output.txt`).

- **Refuses a present top-level `dataset` on a `type: 'joined'` report — RIGHT.** `report.zod.ts:451-460` loops `JOINED_CONTAINER_SELECTION_KEYS` inside the existing joined arm and adds one `custom` issue at `path: [key]`. Probe P2: `{...JOINED, dataset: 'tasks'}` → success=false, exactly one issue, code `custom`, path `dataset`. The renderer at the pin never reads it: joined branch opens at `DatasetReportRenderer.tsx:1462` and returns at `:1526`; the first top-level `report.dataset` read is `:1537`. Matches the file's own contract (`:344-345` docblock, `:443-450` refinement comment) and the card's landing site.
- **Refuses a NON-EMPTY top-level `rows` / `columns` / `values` on a joined report — RIGHT.** Probe P3: three issues, one per key, each at its own path with the prescription. Probe P4 (all four + `order`): five issues in declaration order; the `order` message is byte-identical to main (`a \`joined\` report orders per block — move \`order\` onto \`blocks[]\`.`, `:464`). Ablation claim in the PR body is plausible and the test file pins each refusal by code + path + message; I re-ran the file: 63 passed (13 new).
- **Empty `rows: []` / `columns: []` / `values: []` still parse on a joined container — RIGHT, and deliberate.** Probe P5 → success=true. The threshold is the sibling `order` refusal's own (`r.order?.length`, `:461`); an empty list carries no dropped intent, and refusing it would have broken any GUI draft that pre-seeds empty arrays. The card asked for the four keys to be refused and did not rule on emptiness; the choice is pinned by a test so it reads as a decision, not an omission.
- **`runtimeFilter` and `drilldown` on a joined container still parse — RIGHT.** Probe P6 → success=true, values round-trip. These are exactly the two container keys the joined branch reads (`DatasetReportRenderer.tsx:1455` `mergeFilters(report.runtimeFilter, …)`, `:1457` `report.drilldown`).
- **Non-joined reports untouched — RIGHT.** Probe P12 (no `type`, defaults to `tabular`, with `dataset`/`values`/`blocks`) → success=true; P13 (`matrix` with all four keys) → success=true. The loop sits inside `if (r.type === 'joined')` and the non-joined arm still runs `checkReportOrder` (`:468-470`).
- **Alias routes `measures`→`values`, `dataSet`→`dataset`, `groupings`→`rows` reach the refusal — RIGHT, as a two-step.** Probe P8/P9/P10: the alias key is refused as `unrecognized_keys` naming the rename target (Zod 4 aborts the payload on `unrecognized_keys`, so the superRefine does not run in that same parse — P8 shows `dataset: 'tasks'` beside `measures` is NOT reported until `measures` is fixed). After the rename the target meets the joined refusal (P2/P3). This is the same two-step `sort`→`order` already gives on a joined report (`:308-311` comment), and the alias tables are unchanged. Not a defect; noted as a UX limit in ③.
- **`chart` on a joined container is still accepted — acceptable, out of the card's four keys.** Probe P7 → success=true. The PR declines to refuse it because the natural prescription `blocks[].chart` is itself never rendered at the pin (`git grep -F block.chart` over objectui `packages/` at `f8a9d0fb` → 0 hits; I re-ran it). Reported by the PR as finding 1 for a separate card; correct handling.
- **Every door is the same schema — RIGHT.** `getMetadataTypeSchema('report') === ReportSchema` (probe P16 → true; `metadata-type-schemas.ts:115`), so the save door (`protocol.ts:6625`) and the read-side `_diagnostics` (`metadata-diagnostics.ts:60,100`) carry the same issue; `stack.zod.ts:381` `reports: z.array(ReportSchema)` covers `defineStack` / `os validate` / `os build`; `defineReport` and `Report.create` throw the prescription (P17/P18 → true). The migration entry's WHICH DOOR paragraph is accurate.
- **Refusal text is a correct prescription.** `a \`joined\` report selects per block — move \`KEY\` onto \`blocks[]\`, or delete it; on the container it selects nothing.` — both remedies are true (blocks declare all four keys, `report.zod.ts:231-237`; deleting changes nothing rendered), and "taking the advice parses" is pinned (the matrix-block test). Probe P11 (a plain report flipped to `joined` with no blocks) yields `blocks` needed + `dataset` + `values` refusals together — informative, not contradictory.
- **Public surface unchanged — RIGHT.** `JOINED_CONTAINER_SELECTION_KEYS` is module-private (`:252`, not exported; `ui/index.ts` untouched). Only TSDoc on the four keys changed; no `.describe()` or `.meta()` string changed, so the JSON Schema / reference artefacts are byte-identical. Check-runs: `Lint & Repo Gates` success, `Type Check · source gates` success (lint.yml carries `check:api-surface` at `:6510` and `check:generated --reconcile-only` at `:5453`), `Spec property liveness` success. `liveness/report.json` needs no edit: the four props stay `live` (they are every non-joined report's selection) and their notes already say "for non-joined reports".
- **Producer census — verified, zero container keys anywhere.** My own scan (same-indent sibling keys around every `type: 'joined'`): objectstack head 15 sites / 0 flagged (showcase 1, docs 1, `packages/lint` 3 fixtures, `packages/platform-objects` 2 fixtures, spec tests), objectui at the pin 18 lines / 0 flagged (the PR's "13 occurrences" counts fixtures + docs; CHANGELOG hits make up the difference), cloud `48d7066` → `git grep` exit 1 with the `summary` control exit 0.
- **Nothing refused that should parse; nothing the card names still accepted.** Coverage of the card's four keys is complete; the `order` message is unchanged; no non-joined path is touched.

CI at review time (head check-runs, fetched twice): 25 success, 6 skipped, 0 failure; 6 still `in_progress` — `Test Core (1,3,4,5,6/6)` and `Type Check · workspace`. `Test Core (2/6)`, `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Spec property liveness` concluded success. The seat should confirm the remaining shards before enqueue; nothing in the diff can redden them that the single-file run and the source-gate lane did not already exercise.

### ② Semver level

- **Level: `@objectstack/spec: minor` — RIGHT under the launch-window convention.** The change narrows `ReportSchema`'s accept set (breaking). `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses `major` before GA and its header names the BREAKING banner + ADR-0087 disposition as the carriers; `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml:753-760` (WHICH LEVEL) confirms a breaking change ships as `minor`, and `fix(` may raise a bump but not lower it. Spec is at `17.4.0`; `Check Changeset` (job `changeset-check`, which runs both `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base MERGE_BASE` at `:940` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base MERGE_BASE` at `:1075`) concluded success.
- **Declaration consistent and truthful.** Changeset body carries (a) `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, (b) a `**BREAKING**` banner, (c) a FROM → TO block with the exact old acceptance and the new issue envelope, (d) the one-line fix, (e) exactly one marker `adr-0087: registered ui-report-joined-container-selection-refused`. `readClause2Line` (the single reader, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`) parses both the changeset and the PR body as `{kind: declared, value: no, arm: narrowing}` — I ran it. The claim comment carried the bare `no`; the PR body's `no (narrowing)` is the AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 spelling for a breaking narrowing and is the arm `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` signal (4) reads; the dev declared this deviation in the os-dev report. Consistent.
- **ADR-0087 registration — consistent.** New entry `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-report-joined-container-selection-refused.ts` exports `entry: SemanticMigration` with the id the marker names; `registry.ts` step18 gains the identical object (48 lines) at its sorted position (`ui-reference-rail…` → `ui-report-joined…` → `view-filter-rule…`). I checked the whole step18 list: 170 ids, sorted order equals file order, and the `entries/semantic/18.*` directory holds 170 files — the generator's derived order is respected. Major 18 does not project into `spec-changes.json` / the upgrade guide yet (spec is 17.x), so those artefacts are correctly untouched.
- **Entry content matches the change.** `surface` names the four keys on a joined container with the NON-EMPTY threshold; `replacement` gives both remedies and says `order`'s refusal is unchanged; `reason` cites the pin sha and the renderer lines (`:1462`, `:1529`) — I verified both at `f8a9d0fb` — plus the alias tables (all listed aliases exist in `report.zod.ts:289-301`) and the Studio path (`ReportDefaultInspector.tsx:328` `datasetBound = reportType !== 'joined'`, `:391` `onPatch({ type: v })`, `:530` `hiddenFields` — all verified at the pin); `acceptanceCriteria` names the doors correctly and the census numbers match mine. One nit, not blocking: `surface` is prose rather than the dotted-path style `types.ts:39` suggests, which matches the neighbouring step18 entries' practice.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **PR flag 1 — joined-report charts never render (container or `blocks[].chart`).** Answered: out of the card's scope; verified at the pin (0 `block.chart` reads; container chart read at `:1557` sits after the joined return). Needs its own card (class b, fix shape undecided: render block charts vs retire the key). Not blocking.
- **PR flag 2 — Studio's report type picker leaves a hidden container binding on a draft switched to `joined`; after this PR that save is refused at `dataset`.** Answered: real, verified at the pin (`ReportDefaultInspector.tsx:391` patches only `type`; `:328`/`:530` hide the five keys). The refusal is located and recoverable through the JSON source tab (`ResourceEditPage.tsx:1152` at the pin). objectui is read-only on this card, so the fix (clear or surface the container keys when the type becomes `joined`) needs an objectui card; the seat should file or route it before or with landing. Not blocking — the alternative (keep silently dropping) is the defect the card names.
- **Same hazard exists on this repo's own form, unflagged by the PR:** `packages/spec/src/ui/report.form.ts:37` hides the whole "Dataset binding" section with `visibleWhen: "data.type != 'joined'"` and `:67` shows blocks only for joined — so any SchemaForm consumer of the spec form (not just objectui's inspector) hides stale `dataset` / `rows` / `columns` / `values` on a type switch. Nothing to change in this PR (a visibility rule produces no values), but the objectui card above should name this form as the shared cause so the fix clears the keys rather than only un-hiding them in one inspector.
- **Stored `sys_metadata` rows:** the entry says a stored joined report carrying the keys is not rewritten, shows the issue in `_diagnostics`, and is refused on its next save. Verified: `computeMetadataDiagnostics` re-parses the served document with the same schema (`metadata-diagnostics.ts:60,100`); census finds zero such rows in any seed / example / fixture in the three repos, so no deployment shipped by this repo starts failing. Answered.
- **Alias UX limit (from ① P8):** on a joined report the unknown-key hint sends an author to a key that is then refused, so the full answer is two parses. Same as the existing `sort`→`order` route; a per-key `guidance` entry cannot condition on `type`. Acceptable; a future improvement would be a joined-aware hint in the refinement itself. No escalation.
- **Docs drift:** `content/docs/ui/reports.mdx:105-108` still lists only `order` as the container-only refusal on a joined report — true but now incomplete. Outside the claim's file surface; the PR reports it with no carrier. Suggest the seat attach it to the next docs pass. Not blocking.
- **`ReportSchema.blocks` TSDoc** (`report.zod.ts:403-411`) still describes the pre-cutover block shape (`object`, `groupings`, container `filter`). Pre-existing, noted by the PR, no carrier; not blocking.
- **Nothing found that the author should have flagged and did not**, beyond the `report.form.ts` visibility note above. No producer in objectstack, objectui-at-pin or cloud writes the four keys on a joined container; `analytics-reconcile` reads `blocks` only; `packages/lint` `validate-chart-bindings.ts:539-556` would resolve a container `dataset` on a joined report if one were present, but only to lint it, and none exists.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-19856-joined-report-selection-keys`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Rjy9MeetSfq34PKn81CRiN`

**VERDICT: PASS**
